title: Power Rankings: Heat, Hornets are this week's movers and shakers
heading: 2005-06 Power Rankings: Week 7

rankings.summaryHtml: The near-perfect start just got a little closer to perfect: To go with its sparkly record, Detroit gets to watch its two main East rivals deal with drama earlier than expected.

rankings.summaryHtml: Avery's first 41 regular-season games in charge produced a 33-8 start -- and this season's launch, on its own, ain't bad, either. Dallas, remember, hasn't played a single game yet with its full squad.

rankings.summaryHtml: Hard to imagine a better Manu insurance policy than Finley. But a string of tight games with Manu out  suggests Spurs lack an edge no matter how hot his stand-in is.

rankings.summaryHtml: Perhaps the honeymoon isn't all the way over. Clips just beat hot Houston, welcomed Livingston back from injury and still -- still! -- cling to first place in the Pacific.

rankings.summaryHtml: If nothing else, Riles has a division title in his future. Heat's effort was so much better in his first four games that the Southeast is pretty much clinched already.

rankings.summaryHtml: During the recent three-game skid, with Pau in a funk, Grizz averaged only 76 ppg. Even with their stingy defense, you've got to score at least 86.

rankings.summaryHtml: Bucks would be more inclined to celebrate the fact that they've already matched last season's seven road wins if they hadn't lost both home games last week with some uncharacteristically frigid 3-point shooting (6 for 36).

rankings.summaryHtml: Before you totally dismiss Indy's contender status, don't forget that playing without Artest is not exactly new ground. Pacers have won without him before and still have top-five talent, no matter what they get in a trade.

rankings.summaryHtml: Eight (wins in a row) was definitely not enough. Cavs are 4-7 since and looked so jittery Saturday that they nearly let weary Miami back into a game that was over.
